title: The ADM — The Heart of TOGAF

blocks.text: SESSION 1 — Concept · Key Points · Memory Technique. Read, absorb, stop.
1. Concept Explained Simply

The ADM — Architecture Development Method — is TOGAF's core method. Picture it as a clock face — a circle of phases with Requirements Management at the centre, continuously feeding into every phase. The cycle is iterative — you don't do it once and stop. Critical: The ADM does NOT mandate a specific sequence and does NOT mandate waterfall. It is a reference model, adapted to your context.
2. Key Points — The 10 ADM Elements

rows: Are we ready to do architecture?
What are we trying to achieve?
What data and apps are needed?
How do we get there step by step?
Are projects building what we designed?
How do we manage ongoing change?

blocks.text: 3. Memory Technique

"Prepare → Agree Vision → Build business case → Create systems plan → Design tech → Explore options → Finalise migration → Govern the build → Handle changes."

Three bookends: Preliminary = SETTING UP · Phase A = STARTING every cycle · Phase H = SUSTAINING the architecture.
EXAM TRAP 1 — PHASE G IS NOT PROJECT MANAGEMENT. Phase G is Implementation Governance. The EA team reviews architectural compliance — they do not run projects.
EXAM TRAP 2 — REQUIREMENTS MANAGEMENT IS NOT PHASE I. It is a continuous process at the centre of the ADM — not a ninth sequential phase.
EXAM TRAP 3 — ADM IS NOT WATERFALL. Phases can be revisited, iterated, and run in parallel. Flexibility ≠ skipping critical work.
✋ PAUSE POINT — CHECK BEFORE CONTINUING. Answer from memory before reading Session 2.
1. Where does Requirements Management sit in the ADM, and why does it matter?
At the centre of the ADM cycle — it is a continuous process, not a phase. It operates throughout all phases, managing, storing, and feeding requirements into every part of the ADM.
2. What is Phase G responsible for, and what is it explicitly NOT responsible for?
Phase G (Implementation Governance) reviews architectural compliance — ensuring projects are building what was designed. It is NOT responsible for project management or running delivery projects.
3. Name the three "bookend" phases and what each one does.

Preliminary = sets up the EA practice before any cycle begins. Phase A = starts every ADM cycle (scope, vision, approval). Phase H = sustains the architecture by monitoring for change and triggering new cycles.
SESSION 2 — Real-World Example · Practice Questions · Part 2 Scenario
4. Real-World Example — ServiceNow ITSM mapped to the ADM

items: **Preliminary**: Set up steering committee, agreed ITIL as framework, appointed Programme Architect, set ground rules.
**Phase A**: Scope defined (Incident, Change, Problem, Request). Stakeholders mapped. Vision: "Single unified ITSM platform replacing 4 tools." Statement of Architecture Work approved by CTO.
**Phase B**: Current-state process maps drawn. Target-state processes defined (aligned to ITIL v4). CAB structure agreed.
**Phase C**: Data — CMDB taxonomy defined. Application — ServiceNow modules selected, integration points mapped.
**Phase D**: ServiceNow SaaS on AWS Sydney, MID Server on-prem, TLS 1.3, Azure AD for SSO.
**Phase E**: Three workstreams defined — Core ITSM, CMDB build, integrations. Work Packages confirmed.
**Phase F**: Phased rollout — Wave 1: Incident & Request. Wave 2: Change & Problem. Wave 3: HRSD.
**Phase G**: Architecture review at each wave gate. Compliance checks against integration standards.
**Phase H**: New requirement post-go-live — integrate ServiceNow with Teams. Phase H evaluates whether this needs a new ADM cycle.

blocks.text: 5. Part 1 Practice Questions
Q1. Which phase is primarily concerned with obtaining approval to proceed, identifying stakeholders, and defining scope?

items: A) Preliminary
B) Phase A ✓
C) Phase B
D) Phase E

blocks.text: Answer: B — Phase A is the entry point of every ADM cycle.
Q2. Which statement about Requirements Management is correct?

items: A) It is Phase I, executed after Phase H
B) It is a continuous process at the centre of the ADM cycle ✓
C) It is only performed during Phases A and B
D) It is optional

blocks.text: Answer: B — continuous, not sequential, not optional.
Q3. An EA is reviewing whether a proposed cloud platform complies with designs from Phases B, C, and D. Which phase?

items: A) Phase E
B) Phase F
C) Phase G ✓
D) Phase H

blocks.text: Answer: C — Phase G is specifically about architectural compliance review during implementation.
6. Part 2 Scenario Question (Exam-Authentic Format)

SCENARIO: GlobalTech is in Phase E. The infrastructure team has already selected Azure and signed a three-year contract. The delivery manager says: "Can we just skip Phase D — Technology Architecture — and go straight to planning the migration?"

rows: Agree — ADM allows flexibility and Azure has been selected. Partially right on flexibility but wrong in practice — skipping Phase D means no validated Technology Architecture exists.
Decline — all phases must be completed in strict sequence. Contradicts TOGAF directly.

Acknowledge the Azure selection partially addresses concerns, but Phase D must still be completed — to formally document the Technology Architecture, validate it against Phases B and C, and identify gaps or constraints the contract may have introduced. Best answer.
Escalate to Architecture Board and suspend all work. Disproportionate for a routine delivery situation.
